The agent talks the plan, the
structure and the bug over with
DeepSeek like with a senior
colleague. Not a paid API: your
own free web account.

svg.text: Has it write the hard code

text.tspan: An algorithm, a parser, tricky
logic: asked with a signature,
examples and limits, with
DeepThink on for that message.
Then it reads, fits and tests the
code.
When the answer depends on a new
library version or a changed API,
DeepSeek's web search goes on for
that message: no code from stale
knowledge.
When the work is done it sends the
overall structure, then each file
in its own message, and applies
the fixes. A second pair of eyes
for you.
A local model, OpenCode's free
big-pickle or Claude Code: it does
the work and gets DeepSeek's help
where it gets stuck.
Messages go in plain words, spaced
out and capped. A message holding
a password, token or key is
not sent; .c2fignore files stay
out.
Debug layer. Every program the agent writes gets a debug layer behind one switch (APP_DEBUG=1); on an error it finds
the block, and asks DeepSeek about that block if it can't solve it.
One session, one chat. Every consult of an agent session runs in a single DeepSeek chat; you can read what was asked
and answered.
No blind copying. It doesn't use code it doesn't understand, and asks you before a command that installs, deletes,
downloads or changes system settings.
No consults for small things. A short question or a one-line fix sends nothing.
DeepSeek never sees your files; it reads only what the agent writes to it. The agent does the work; the advisor gives
opinions, explanations and, when asked, code.
Make a notes app: notes live in one JSON file and the find command finds them.
The folder is empty. Plan: notes.js (commands), store.js (storage), search.js (search). I'm talking
storage over before I write it.
I'll keep the notes in a single JSON file. What happens if two commands write at the same time, do
you think I need a lock?
No lock needed: write to a temp file first, then rename it over the real one. Even if a write is cut
off, the file stays intact. One of two notes written at the same moment can be lost; for a
single-user CLI that's acceptable.
store.js writes through a temp file + rename, tests pass. Search is the hard part; I'm having that
one written.
I need search(notes, query): every word of the query must match the start of a word in the note,
ignoring case and accents. Example: cafe → "Café notes".
Strip accents and lowercase, then compare word starts:
const norm = (s) => s.normalize("NFD").replace(/\p{M}/gu, "").toLowerCase();
export function search(notes, query) {
const words = norm(query).split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
return notes.filter((n) => {
const heads = norm(n.text).split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u);
return words.every((w) => heads.some((h) => h.startsWith(w)));
search.js is in; all tests pass, cafe → "Café notes" included. Done, now the file-by-file review,
starting with store.js.

Kur.bat also puts c2f on your user PATH (no admin rights) and gives OpenCode c2f, the ctf agent, the /ctf_ask command
and the session plugin.
Each computer signs in on its own. A login is bound to the computer it was taken on; a copy is refused. Your friends
sign in with their own DeepSeek accounts.
Moved the folder? Run Kur.bat once more in the new place; c2f durum tells you.
Update: c2f guncelle (installed from a ZIP? Unzip the new one into the same folder, then Kur.bat).
OpenCode
Kur.bat connects it. New sessions open with the ctf agent; pick any model and type. From
another agent, once: /ctf_ask your request.

In the MCP settings: "c2f": { "command": "node", "args": ["<folder>/src/mcp.js"] }. Give
tools a timeout of at least 5 minutes.

MIT license
# never goes to DeepSeek
secrets/
config/prod.json
*billing*.py
Put a .c2fignore in the project folder (like .gitignore). A message
holding lines from those files is not sent; the agent describes them in
its own words. If a huge project can't be checked file by file, the
message is not sent either. A file with just off in it means c2f never
consults in that project: for fully private work such as company code.
Protect your account. DeepSeek's web chat is not an API. An account was suspended while this project drove
it like a machine (25 messages and 14 new chats in 11 minutes). So c2f only consults: in plain words, capped
and spaced out. The only risk-free way is DeepSeek's paid official API.
Message length
30,000 characters (DeepSeek's own cap is about 40,000)
Between two messages
at least 15 s
Between two new chats
at least 2 min
Bursts
at most 10 per 10 minutes; more waits (sites.deepseek.limit.burstMax /
burstMinutes)
Secrets
a message holding a password, API key, token or private key is not sent; the
agent is asked for a placeholder such as <API_KEY>
Same message
not sent again within 10 min
"Too frequent"
retried in the same chat after 30 / 60 / 120 s; then a 10 min rest
Quota used up
never retried; the agent says when it reopens and finishes the work on its own
The old features that drive DeepSeek like a model or an API (build, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, c2f_chat) are off
(automation); turning them on is not advised.
c2f uses no browser fingerprinting or any other detection evasion.
The agent says there's no c2f_advise tool
c2f kur, then a new session
c2f durum points at an old folder
The folder moved: c2f kur in the new place
Login taken on another computer / expired
"DeepSeek asked to slow down"
A short wait; the agent keeps working and consults again after the
given time
Quota used up
Wait for the reopening time; the agent finishes on its own
One session opened a second DeepSeek chat
The agent didn't pass the thread id: add the c2f kurallar output to
its instructions
All under %LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatToFree\, on this computer
only. deepseek-auth.json is your login and worth as
much as a password: never share, copy or commit it.
sent.log keeps no message text.
